summary.name: Apple Silicon App Test
summary.one_liner: A beta web tool that scans a Mac app or zip file to check whether it has native Apple Silicon compatibility.
keywords: does this app run on m1
does this app run on m5 mac
intel to apple silicon app check
check app before buying new mac
use_cases: Check whether a Mac app runs natively before buying an Apple Silicon Mac
Find out if an app needs Rosetta 2 translation
Scan a zipped Mac app to see its Apple Silicon status
Check app compatibility from Windows, Linux, or iOS by uploading a Mac app file
summary.what_it_does: The tool scans Mac apps and zip files containing Mac apps to determine whether they have native Apple Silicon support. Apps reported as non-native are marked with an orange diamond, meaning no native build has been reported yet, though they may still run under Rosetta 2. The page says DMG and PKG files must be extracted first, except for certain rare DMG files. Larger files take longer to scan, and some apps may cause the scan to hang. The page also notes that Rosetta 2 behavior cannot be tested through a website alone, so a manual review is suggested for that question.
notable: Scans Mac app binaries in the browser to report Apple Silicon (native) status
Flags non-native apps that may still work under Rosetta 2
Open-source project (listed as open source in awesome-mac, linking to the ThatGuySam/doesitarm GitHub repo)
Offers a manual review request for Rosetta 2 status
caveats: Cannot test Rosetta 2 compatibility without a physical Apple Silicon Mac; the page says human review is the best method for that
Some apps can make the scan hang indefinitely
Only Mac Apps, zip files containing Mac apps, and specific rare DMG files are supported; DMG and PKG files generally must be extracted first
